rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 12 mm apart across x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, with 12 mm footprints, so the tape (25 mm) always covers at least one or two sensors. They sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the line. A 0.12 m wheel track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.12 m body width and 0.8 kg mass give moderate yaw inertia and a body width that keeps the off-track limit at max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m. Controller: sensor weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] match sensor x order, so a line on the left (positive signal) steers left. base_speed 1.4 (about 70% PWM) should give the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed, while leaving room to slow down on tight bends. kp 2.0 gives a moderate steering response (a full-scale signal of 2 gives turn 4, about 1400 PWM difference). ki 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd 0.1 damps oscillation without amplifying sensor noise much. line_loss 'last_direction' lets the robot recover in the direction it was heading when it lost the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. Hypotheses to test: (1) if steering_oscillation is high, reduce kp or raise kd; (2) if completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed toward 1.8; (3) if the robot drifts off the line on the slalom, raise kp or add sensor spread. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error and max_error give the tracking quality; line_loss_events shows recovery frequency; steering_oscillation shows jitter.
